gen-dafont-eraser-gf-rokkitt: Fat stylus-width strokes with no swelling anywhere, understated yet commanding. Rokkitt, a serif with a wide-mouthed c, gives running text a bookish, traditional pace that carries on comfortably down the page.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-sanchez: Understated, yet commanding: Eraser keeps every stroke one plotter-pen line. Below it, Sanchez lends dignified, bookish text with a c opened like calipers, giving the single-weight heading a studied partner.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-solway: Bold, flat-weighted letters with a quiet, commanding presence up top, with no swelling strokes. And Solway lends an authoritative, bookish voice underneath, its e opening generously into the eye.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-yuji-boku: Heavy, hushed, uniform lines, understated but commanding from the first word. Yuji Boku brings an editorial, dignified voice, each stroke holding one thickness and its c swung wide open, so long text glides along.
gen-dafont-eraser-nunito-sans: Eraser draws bold, rope-like lines that never thicken or thin. Where Eraser is best at commanding a single line, Nunito Sans, a soft sans-serif with open-mouthed curves, is best at carrying the text.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-amulya: The text here reads contemporary and modern, its curves keeping their gaps generous. Amulya, a sans of moderate lowercase height, hands the fast, aggressive spotlight to Ethnocentric, whose letters sit pushed apart.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-chillax: Loud meets lazy: Ethnocentric shouts fast, spaced-out letters, then Chillax trails spaghetti-like lines whose pen-lifted curves leave loops unfinished. Sheer speed set against sheer ease, and the gap is the fun.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-plein: Plein reads reliable and clean, a sans-serif with a clear channel leading into each round letter. But the standout is the height gap, high lowercase in Ethnocentric against moderate in Plein.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads contemporary and approachable, with wide gaps by the curve ends. Ethnocentric does fast, aggressive spectacle, letters pushed apart, while the sans below does quiet, uniform-weight consistency.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-synonym: Synonym is a clean, dependable sans-serif, a plain stripe of constant ink. But the real hook is the lowercase height, high in Ethnocentric and moderate here, which sets the two apart at a glance.
